# Inventory

A real inventory: a player's (`player:inventory()`), their ender chest, a storage of the project's that they keep (`player:storage(name, size)`), a container block's (`block:inventory()`: a chest, a barrel, a hopper, a furnace) or an entity's (a chest boat, a donkey, a villager). Its item methods work like `Menu`'s. The handle is where the inventory is, so it reads live; once that's gone (a chest broken, a player offline, a chunk unloaded) its methods answer `nil`, `false` or nothing. Slots are numbered from 0. A player's: the hotbar 0 to 8, the rest of the main inventory 9 to 35, armour 36 (feet), 37 (legs), 38 (chest) and 39 (head), the offhand 40, then body armour 41 and a saddle 42 (what the game keeps there for any entity). A double chest's inventory is both halves, 0 to 53.

A handle: call its methods with a colon, `inventory:method()`.

## The inventory {#the-inventory}

### `inventory:exists()` {#exists}

Whether it's there now: the player online, the container still a container, the entity in the world and its chunk loaded.

**Returns** `boolean`

### `inventory:kind()` {#kind}

What kind of inventory it is: `"player"`, `"ender_chest"`, `"storage"`, `"chest"`, `"barrel"`, `"shulker_box"`, `"hopper"`, `"dispenser"`, `"dropper"`, `"furnace"`, `"brewing"`, … `nil` once it's gone.

**Returns** `string?`

### `inventory:size()` {#size}

How many slots it has: 43 for a player, 27 for a chest, 54 for a double chest. 0 once it's gone.

**Returns** `integer`

### `inventory:holder()` {#holder}

Whose it is: the `Player` (for a player's inventory, ender chest and storage), the `Entity`, or the `Block`. `nil` once it's gone.

**Returns** [`Entity`](entity.md)`\|`[`Block`](block.md)`\|nil`

### `inventory:viewers()` {#viewers}

The players who have it open on their screen now: for a storage, those looking at a window with a slot bound to it. (A player's own inventory, open in their own inventory screen, doesn't count: the server can't tell.)

**Returns** [`Player`](player.md)`[]`

## Slots {#slots}

### `inventory:item(index)` {#item}

What is in a slot, or `nil` for an empty one (or once it's gone). A slot outside it is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` | From 0. |

**Returns** [`Item`](types.md#item)`?`

### `inventory:set_item(index, item?)` {#set_item}

Puts an item in a slot, replacing what was there, or empties it. A slot outside it, an item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` | From 0. |
| `item` (optional) | [`Item`](types.md#item) | Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it's gone.

### `inventory:items()` {#items}

Every item in it, keyed by slot. Empty slots are left out, so `pairs` visits only what is there.

**Returns** `table<integer, `[`Item`](types.md#item)`>`

```lua
for index, item in pairs(player:inventory():items()) do
  log(index, item.kind, item.count)
end
```

### `inventory:clear()` {#clear}

Empties every slot. To empty one, `set_item(index, nil)`.

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it's gone.

## Adding and finding items {#adding-and-finding-items}

### `inventory:add_item(item)` {#add_item}

Puts an item wherever it fits, topping up matching stacks first, the way picking something up does. In a player's inventory only the hotbar and main inventory take it, never armour or the offhand.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | [`Item`](types.md#item) |  |

**Returns** `integer`: How many didn't fit: 0 when all of it went in, all of it once the inventory's gone.

### `inventory:remove_item(match, count?)` {#remove_item}

Takes away items that match, from the first slot on, until `count` are gone or none are left.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | `string\|`[`ItemMatch`](types.md#itemmatch) | An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error. |
| `count` (optional) | `integer` | How many at most. Leave it out for every one that matches. |

**Returns** `integer`: How many it took.

```lua
local taken = player:inventory():remove_item({ kind = "minecraft:gold_nugget", data = { coin = true } }, 10)
```

### `inventory:count_item(match)` {#count_item}

How many items match, across every slot.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | `string\|`[`ItemMatch`](types.md#itemmatch) | An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error. |

**Returns** `integer`

### `inventory:has_item(match, count?)` {#has_item}

Whether at least `count` items match.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | `string\|`[`ItemMatch`](types.md#itemmatch) | An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error. |
| `count` (optional) | `integer` | Default 1. |

**Returns** `boolean`

### `inventory:first_slot(match)` {#first_slot}

The first slot holding an item that matches, or `nil` when none does.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | `string\|`[`ItemMatch`](types.md#itemmatch) | An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error. |

**Returns** `integer?`
